note: The woken dead of the old kings' tomb. Its people are tools/worlds/homelands.json's (Tomb of Kings): Elder Ossric, in the great hall, gives the first two; Captain Harrow, a few steps from him, the three hunts; Shroudmaker Corwen, up the hall on its east side, is the outfitter; Coachman Grimsby keeps the stable in the middle of the hall to the north (his coach, a hearse once, runs to Freeport and to the other homes). The tomb's doors do not open in the client, so the hunts are down the great hall's own passage to the south: the tomb beetles in the excavators' pit, the crypt bats in the passage beyond it, the living grave robber Sela at its far end.

L1.name: A Waking Band
offer: So. Another of us opens eyes it no longer has. Be still a moment. The first waking is the strangest.
Each of the woken wears a band of the kings' bronze, so the sentinels do not take you for a robber. Shroudmaker Corwen keeps them, up the hall to the north.
Will you fetch your waking band and show it to me?
L1.declined: As you like. We have nothing here if not time.
L1.started: Corwen's alcove is up the hall to the north, on the east side.

piece.name: waking band
piece.description: A band of tarnished bronze from the kings' stores. Each of the woken dead of the tomb wears one.

fetch.journal: Ask Shroudmaker Corwen, up the hall north of Elder Ossric, for a waking band.
fetch.says: Newly woken? Give me your wrist. What is left of it. There: the kings' bronze, and it will not slip. No charge. The dead do not bill the dead.

show.journal: Show the waking band to Elder Ossric.
show.says: It fits, as far as anything fits us now. Wear it, and the tomb will know you for its own.

L2.name: Bound to the Tomb
offer: You have died once. It need not become a habit. Have Spiritmaster Vellum bind you to the tomb, so that you gather yourself here if your bones are scattered.
Then give your name to Coachman Grimsby, up the hall. His coach runs to Freeport and to the other homes of the Homelands.
Will you see them both and come back to me?
L2.declined: Then do try not to fall apart in the meantime.
L2.started: Vellum keeps the alcove to the south-west. Grimsby waits up the hall to the north.

bind.journal: Have Spiritmaster Vellum, in the alcove south-west of the elder, bind your spirit to the tomb.
bind.says: It is done. Wherever your bones fall, they will find their way back here. Now go and give Coachman Grimsby your name.

ledger.journal: Give your name to Coachman Grimsby, up the hall north of the elder, for his ledger.
ledger.says: Another one up and about! My coach was a hearse once. It runs to Freeport and to every other home of the Homelands, for those whose names their ledgers hold. Yours is in mine now.

says: Good. Now even the worst day ends with you back among us.
Grimsby's coach goes where its ledgers know you, but the road to Freeport's guilds is earned. Captain Harrow, beside me, has work for you.

L3.name: Beetles in the Bones
offer: You are the new one. Good. Tomb beetles have come up out of the excavators' pit, down the hall to the south, and they gnaw at those of us who have not woken yet.
Crack them and bring me three of their shells. Then I will show you something every one of the watch should know.
Will you hunt them?
L3.declined: Then the sleepers are gnawed a little longer. They will not complain.
L3.started: Three shells. The pit is down the hall to the south.

drop.name: tomb beetle shell
drop.description: The cracked shell of a tomb beetle from the excavators' pit in the Tomb of Kings.

hunt.journal: Take three tomb beetle shells from the tomb beetles in the pit south of the great hall.

give.journal: Bring three tomb beetle shells to Captain Harrow.
give.says: Three shells, and you are still in one piece. More or less. Now attend, and learn this.

L4.name: Arms for the Woken
offer: Bare bone breaks. I will make you proper gear from the kings' stores, but you will fetch what I need.
Shroudmaker Corwen has cord and a shaft set by for me. Then take a wing from the crypt bats that roost in the south passage, past the pit.
Will you bring me all three?
L4.declined: Then go as you are, and count your ribs afterwards.
L4.started: Cord and a shaft from Corwen, a wing from the bats. Go.

materials.journal: Ask Shroudmaker Corwen for the silk cord and the wooden shaft.
materials.says: For the captain? Here: a length of cord and a straight shaft. Tell him I want the cord back when you have no more use for it. I can wait.

drop.name: crypt bat wing
drop.description: The leathery wing of a crypt bat from the south passage of the Tomb of Kings.

hunt.journal: Take a crypt bat wing from the crypt bats in the passage south of the pit.

give.journal: Bring the silk cord, the wooden shaft and the crypt bat wing to Captain Harrow.
give.says: All three. A moment... there. It is yours. It has outlasted better hands than ours.

L5.name: The Living Robber
offer: One task more. A living robber, Sela by name, has got in at the far end of the south passage and is prying the seals off the kings' doors.
The living strike first when they see us, so do not stand and stare. Put her out, and bring me the seal she stole.
Will you deal with the robber?
L5.declined: She will not grow more honest while you wait.
L5.started: The far end of the south passage. She will see you before you see her.

drop.name: stolen burial seal
drop.description: A seal of old ivory, pried from a king's door by the robber Sela.

hunt.journal: Take the stolen burial seal from Tomb Robber Sela at the far south end of the passage.

give.journal: Bring the stolen burial seal to Captain Harrow.
says: The seal, and whole! The kings may go on sleeping. You have earned your place on the watch.
Learn this, and see Gatekeeper Dustcloak down the hall to the south when you are ready for Freeport.

flight.name: The Road to Freeport
offer: The living fear us, but Freeport is not so particular, and its guilds will train you as they would any other.
You have earned the road, woken one. I will set you down among your own guild in Freeport, and your spirit will rest there.
Shall I send you to Freeport?
flight.declined: The tomb is patient. So am I.
flight.started: Walk tall, and keep your bones together!
flight.journal: Tell Gatekeeper Dustcloak when you are ready to go to Freeport.

L7.name: Claws and Fur
offer: You have stood the watch well. The living keep a hunters' outpost at the Goldfeather Eyrie, and every home sends its young there. The tomb will too.
Ride Grimsby's coach to the Eyrie. Corwen wants drift rat fur to line the shrouds, and I want two badger claws. Both are on the snow east of the outpost.
Will you hunt the Eyrie's snow?
L7.declined: We have time. We have nothing but time.
L7.started: Grimsby's coach will take you. The cold will not trouble you. Small mercies.

drop.name: snowfield badger claw
drop.description: A blunt digging claw from a snowfield badger of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take two snowfield badger claws from the badgers on the snow east of the Eyrie outpost.

drop.name: drift rat fur
drop.description: A clump of white fur from a drift rat of the Goldfeather Eyrie's snow.

hunt.journal: Take a clump of drift rat fur from the drift rats east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the badger claws and the drift rat fur to Captain Harrow.
give.says: Claws and fur. The fur is Corwen's; the claws will make latches the robbers cannot pry. Now attend, and learn this.

L10.name: White Feathers
offer: Your arms are older than you are, which here is saying something. The kings' armourers dressed their best arms in white feathers, and the pale owls of the Eyrie have them.
Corwen has cord and a shaft set by for me again. Then take two feathers from the pale owls north of the Eyrie outpost.
Will you bring me the cord, the shaft and the feathers?
L10.declined: The old arms will do. They have done for centuries.
L10.started: Cord and a shaft from Corwen, feathers from the owls. Go.

materials.journal: Ask Shroudmaker Corwen for another length of silk cord and another wooden shaft.
materials.says: Again? The captain goes through cord the way the living go through bread. Here. I still want the first length back.

drop.name: pale owl feather
drop.description: A long white flight feather from a pale owl of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take two pale owl feathers from the pale owls north of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the silk cord, the wooden shaft and the pale owl feathers to Captain Harrow.
give.says: White feathers, as the kings' armourers used. A moment... there. It is yours. Try to outlast it.

L13.name: The Warden's Asking
offer: Warden Halvek of the Eyrie outpost sent word by Grimsby's coach. The frostpaw cubs north of the outpost, past the river, have grown bold, and his hunters are tired.
He asked for the watch by name. It is not every day the living ask the dead for help. Kill five of the cubs.
Will you answer the warden?
L13.declined: Then the living must wait. They are not good at it.

hunt.journal: Kill five frostpaw cubs north of the Eyrie outpost, past the river.

back.says: Five, and the warden's thanks came by the coach. The living may yet learn to like us. Learn this.

L15.name: A Shard for the Spirits
offer: Spiritmaster Oswin of the Eyrie outpost writes that a thing walks the ice caves north-east of it, the Rimeheart: cold, old and not alive. Rather like us, but less polite.
Break it, and carry a shard to Oswin, so that he can be sure it does not wake again. Then come back to me.
Will you break the Rimeheart?
L15.declined: Then it walks on. Some things do.
L15.started: Go with friends. Even bones can be broken.

drop.name: shard of the Rimeheart
drop.description: A shard of blue ice that never melts, broken from the Rimeheart.

hunt.journal: Take a shard from the Rimeheart, in the ice caves north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

carry.journal: Bring the shard of the Rimeheart to Spiritmaster Oswin at the Eyrie outpost.
carry.says: The Rimeheart's own ice. Nothing stirs in it now. Tell your captain the outpost thanks the tomb. I never thought I would say that.

back.says: Oswin's thanks, to the tomb. The kings would be amused. You have done the watch proud. Learn this.

L20.name: A Watch Among the Living
offer: Harrow says you have earned your place on the watch. Before the woken choose their path, each stands one watch among the living at the Eyrie, so they learn we mean no harm.
Spiritmaster Oswin at the Eyrie outpost knows you now. Go to him, do as the outpost asks, then come back to me and choose your path.
Will you stand watch among the living?
L20.declined: We are patient. It is the one thing death teaches.
L20.started: Go. Try not to frighten anyone.

road.journal: Find Spiritmaster Oswin at the Eyrie outpost.
road.says: The woken one who broke the Rimeheart. The outpost has heard. Scout Feyla, on the river's far reach, needs a steady hand: go to her.

road.journal: Find Scout Feyla on the frozen river, north-east of the Eyrie outpost.
road.says: Oswin sent you? I see. Well, the raiders will run from you if from nothing else. Bring me three of their war-talons.

drop.name: Goldfeather war-talon
drop.description: A war-talon of the Goldfeather aviaks, bound in gold thread.

hunt.journal: Take three war-talons from the Goldfeather raiders round the eyrie east of the Eyrie outpost.

handin.journal: Bring the three war-talons to Scout Feyla.
handin.says: Three talons. I will not pretend you did not startle me, but that was good work. Warden Halvek should hear of it.

after.journal: Tell Warden Halvek at the Eyrie outpost that the raiders are beaten back.
after.says: Feyla speaks well of you, and Feyla speaks well of no one. The tomb is welcome at the Eyrie. Go home, woken one.

final.journal: Return to Elder Ossric in the Tomb of Kings.
final.says: You opened your eyes in this hall not long ago. Now the living know your name, and speak it kindly. The tomb has one thing more for you.

L20.picked: Then it is yours. Spend it well. We of all folk know how short a life is.
